cf.title: ReplicationSlotRelease() clobbers another backend's statusFlags entry

input.subject: ReplicationSlotRelease() clobbers another backend's statusFlags entry

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. Message #1 states the bug, the affected processes and the branch range, and Kuroda confirmed the analysis in message #2. v2-0001 changes one function and adds no user-visible surface. The open points are whether v2-0002 and the TAP test are committed, which the thread is already settling.

brief.title: Stop slot release in auxiliary processes from overwriting another backend's statusFlags
brief.problem: ReplicationSlotRelease() writes MyProc->statusFlags to ProcGlobal->statusFlags[MyProc->pgxactoff], but auxiliary processes are not in the proc array and have pgxactoff 0. When the checkpointer or startup process invalidates a slot, it overwrites the flags of the backend at offset 0. Assert builds crash, and losing PROC_AFFECTS_ALL_HORIZONS on a walsender can let vacuum remove rows a standby still needs.
brief.proposed_design: v2-0001 skips the shared store in ReplicationSlotRelease() unless PROC_IN_LOGICAL_DECODING is set, and adds a TAP test; it is back-patched to v14. v2-0002 adds ProcArrayHasProc() and asserts it wherever a process changes its own statusFlags entry. v1 asserted that AmAuxiliaryProcess() is false instead.
user_visible_surface: C API: new function ProcArrayHasProc() in procarray.h (v2-0002 only).
C API: new macro AmAuxiliaryProcess() in miscadmin.h (v1 only, dropped in v2).
author_claims: Affects every branch from v14 through master; v13 passes the reproducer.
A standby hits the bug during restartpoints, and from v16 during ordinary replay via 26669757b6a.
From v18, idle_replication_slot_timeout can trigger it without max_slot_wal_keep_size.
Nothing changes for processes in the proc array, since only StartupDecodingContext() sets PROC_IN_LOGICAL_DECODING.
Core regression tests and the recovery and subscription TAP suites pass on master with the patch.
brief.thread_state: Kuroda confirmed the analysis; Paquier plans to commit only v2-0001 down to v14 and doubts both the extra assertions and the test. The author replied that the test fails without the fix even without the v2-0002 assertions; CFbot reports the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: The material does not say whether the test will be committed or how the back-branch versions get a local advance_wal() helper.
The proposal does not say whether any production report of standby row loss exists, beyond the analysis.
The test numbering changed from 057 to 058; the material does not say whether it conflicts with existing tests on back branches.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The fix changes ReplicationSlotRelease() in slot.c, reached during slot invalidation by the checkpointer and the startup process on standbys.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: v2-0002 adds ProcArrayHasProc() to procarray.h; v2-0001 adds no API.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: v2-0001 is marked Backpatch-through: 14, and the test needs a local advance_wal() helper before v17.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: v2-0002 adds assertions in six files, and the new TAP test must be kept working on six branches.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is there any production report of a standby losing rows through this path, or does the PROC_AFFECTS_ALL_HORIZONS case rest on analysis only?
Will the TAP test be committed with the fix, and what does the back-branch version use in place of $node->advance_wal() before v17?
Does test number 058 conflict with an existing test in src/test/recovery on any branch from v14 to v18?
Is v2-0002 meant for master only, and does any path besides ReplicationSlotRelease() reach its new assertions from a process outside the proc array?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier takes part in the thread and, per the brief, plans to commit v2-0001 down to v14. The owner needs to know replication slot invalidation and the proc array.
committability.liability: A one-function change in ReplicationSlotRelease() on six branches, v14 through master. If the test is committed, the owner also signs for its stability on the buildfarm on each branch.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 one day after the first review, answered each review point in message #3, and replied again after the committer's comments.

priority.reason: The bug affects installations where the checkpointer or startup process invalidates a slot, on v14 and later, and can weaken hot standby feedback. v2-0001 is a small change in slot.c with a committer engaged; CFbot reports that the patch needs a rebase.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claim that only StartupDecodingContext() sets PROC_IN_LOGICAL_DECODING is taken from the commit message. Messages #4 and #5 were not shown; the committer's plan is taken from the brief.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Restore lock level to update statusFlags
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Restore lock level to update statusFlags
Reverted commit(s): Relax lock level for setting PGPROC->statusFlags
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Reverts 27838981be9d (some comments are kept).  Per discussion, it does
not seem safe to relax the lock level used for this; in order for it to
be safe, there would have to be memory barriers between the point we set
the flag and the point we set the trasaction Xid, which perhaps would
not be so bad; but there would also have to be barriers at the readers'
side, which from a performance perspective might be bad.

Now maybe this analysis is wrong and it *is* safe for some reason, but
proof of that is not trivial.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronous replay mode for avoiding stale reads on hot standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a synchronous_replay mode in which a commit on the primary waits until all available hot standbys have replayed it, and the primary grants time-limited leases to standbys. A standby without a valid lease rejects synchronous_replay transactions with a new error 40P02, so reads on standbys never miss a commit that has already returned on the primary.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible message, from February 2019, is a rebase by the author, and the entry was withdrawn in July 2019. Open items still visible at that point included missing TAP tests, an unexplained replication protocol corruption bug, and design questions from Masahiko Sawada about the GUCs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.
matched_queries: replication slot release single user mode
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add function pg_advance_replication_slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a SQL function that moves a physical replication slot forward to a given WAL position without consuming the WAL, for example to keep slots in sync across servers. Later versions named it pg_advance_replication_slot, allowed forward moves only, and raised an error on logical slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier asked that moving the slot backwards raise an error with the current slot position instead of a warning, and that the logical-slot error use ERRCODE_FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED. Andres Freund added that neither message followed the message style guidelines. The patch got no update in the following two months, so it was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:

reflect that. So I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix assertion failure in SnapBuildInitialSnapshot()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes an assertion failure in SnapBuildInitialSnapshot(), where the snapshot xmin was older than the safe xid from GetOldestSafeDecodingTransactionId(). It changes the locking in ReplicationSlotsComputeRequiredXmin() so that a concurrent call, for example from an apply worker, cannot overwrite procArray->replication_slot_xmin with an older value.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stalled for about a year with no agreement on the locking approach. Andres Freund was concerned about holding ProcArrayLock exclusively while iterating over slots, and Robert Haas asked for data on that cost and suggested making ProcArraySetReplicationSlotXmin() refuse to retreat the value. Nobody answered Robert's points, so the entry was set to Waiting on Author and then returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
ProcArraySetReplicationSlotXmin() could refuse to retreat the values,
perhaps? If it computes an older value than what's there, it just does
nothing?

precedents_retrieved.title: Trigger failsafe when VACUUM is run in single user mode
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a VACUUM option for single-user mode, first called VACUUM LIMIT and later VACUUM (EMERGENCY), that vacuums only tables whose xid or mxid age passes a fixed cutoff, with failsafe behavior and no index cleanup or truncation. The aim is to get out of single-user mode quickly after a wraparound shutdown.
precedents_retrieved.objection: During review, the thread found that the v14 failsafe already turns off heap truncation, so plain VACUUM should work under the postmaster at xidStopLimit. The plan then moved to removing the advice to use single-user mode. Noah Misch then showed that VACUUM can still create multixacts at multiStopLimit, so more work was needed. The author was away sick and withdrew the work for v15.
matched_queries: replication slot release single user mode
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I gather from subsequent discussion that a full solution goes beyond just a new warning message and documentation. Either way I'm not quite prepared to address this in time for v15.

precedents_retrieved.title: skip replication slot snapshot/map file removal during end-of-recovery checkpoint
precedents_retrieved.summary: Skip the enumeration and removal of logical replication snapshot (.snap) and mapping (map-) files during the end-of-recovery checkpoint, so the server becomes available sooner, and leave the files to the next regular checkpoint. A GUC could control this, with the current behavior as the default.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Nathan Bossart argued that skipping the files only at end of recovery does not solve the problem, because regular checkpoints stay slow and the shutdown or end-of-recovery checkpoint can still take a long time. He proposed moving these tasks out of checkpointing, which another thread was already discussing. The author agreed to handle the problem in that thread and withdrew this entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If
there are frequently many such files to delete and regular checkpoints
are taking longer, the shutdown/end-of-recovery checkpoint could still
take a while.  I think it would be better to separate these tasks from
checkpointing instead.

precedents_retrieved.title: base backup client as auxiliary backend process
precedents_retrieved.summary: The postmaster starts an auxiliary process that takes a base backup from the primary when it finds a basebackup.signal file in a minimal data directory created by initdb, then continues startup in standby mode. Connection settings come from postgresql.conf, so setting up a standby no longer needs pg_basebackup.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry because he could not finish it, and said the order of startup actions in postmaster.c needed more thinking. Andres Freund's review had questioned the polling wait loop in PostmasterMain, missing error and signal handling in the base backup process, the handling of shutdown during the backup, and putting the backup code in libpqwalreceiver.c. Some refactoring parts were committed separately.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Unsurprisingly, the sequencing of startup actions in postmaster.c is
extremely tricky and needs more thinking.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix cancelled queries when hot_standby_feedback = on
precedents_retrieved.summary: With hot_standby_feedback = on, standby queries still get cancelled when vacuum truncates a heap on the primary, because the AccessExclusiveLock taken for truncation is replayed on the standby. The final patch adds a new lock level, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE LOCAL, that vacuum uses for heap truncation and that is not WAL-logged, so standby queries must tolerate concurrent truncation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane showed that letting scans run during truncation leaves a race: concurrent scans can load to-be-truncated pages back into shared buffers before ftruncate, and reading past EOF on a standby can extend the relation. Alexander Korotkov agreed the patch had to be revised and sketched a new truncation design, but Robert Haas called it fragile and doubted it prevents stale buffers from being taken as valid. No new version followed, the existing patch failed initdb, and the entry was closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If we ever have valid-looking buffers in shared_buffers after the corresponding data has been truncated away on disk, we've got to make sure that nobody ever confuses one of them with an actually-valid buffer.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found; the corpus returned no row for the same or a similar idea. Message #1 points to a related v14-only report of the same assertion through a different route (a stale walsender pgxactoff), where nothing was committed, and to a single-user-mode fix of ReplicationSlotRelease(). Neither is a rejection of this idea, and the committer in message #4 plans to commit v2-0001 down to v14.

Nothing in my angle applies. The fix changes no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog, pg_dump output, psql behaviour or client-visible protocol. The only behaviour change stops a write to another backend's statusFlags entry. The new ProcArrayHasProc() is an internal assertion helper in v2-0002, and the committer plans to skip that patch. Test numbering on back branches is a commit-time detail.

The fix touches only shared-memory state in ProcGlobal->statusFlags. It changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol or back-branch ABI, and it removes a path that could weaken hot standby feedback. v2-0002 adds ProcArrayHasProc(), but it is master-only and Paquier plans to commit just v2-0001.

The fix adds no new privilege, role, setting or user-visible surface; it removes a wrong shared-memory store made by the checkpointer or startup process. Reaching the bug path takes slot setup and server configuration, and the fix only narrows exposure, so the security angle has no objection.

From the maintenance angle this is a narrow bug fix in one function: v2-0001 adds no API, GUC, catalog change or hot-path cost. Michael Paquier, a committer in this area, plans to commit only v2-0001 down to v14 (message #4), which settles the v2-0002 assertions and the new ProcArrayHasProc() API. The back-branch test, which needs a local advance_wal() helper before v17, is a level-4 matter and outside scope.

This is a bug fix for a wrong-index store in ReplicationSlotRelease(), and no existing feature, setting or extension can stand in for a correct core fix. The added ProcArrayHasProc() assertion helper is closest to duplicating existing checks, but it is not a second mechanism for a user-facing job, and Paquier already plans to drop it (message #4).

This is a bug fix, so demand is not in doubt. The author found it from a real CI crash on a primary while autovacuum ran (message #1), Kuroda reproduced and confirmed it (message #2), and a committer plans to back-patch v2-0001 to v14 (message #4). The fix adds no user-visible surface. Whether v2-0002 and the test belong in the commit is a design and test question, outside the demand angle.
